verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. `integral_equal_after` is exactly the paper's propagation, one cumulative integral at a time: with B = X_h, its `hanchor` is Δ(row)(X_h,η) = 0, its `htail` is the agreement of the integrands on [X_h,X] that the paper deduces from (U_1,E_1) = (U_2,E_2) there, and its conclusion is Δ(row)(X,η) = 0 for X ≥ X_h. Two differences of packaging. (a) The paper asserts it for the 5-tuple 𝔪 = (M,I,J,S,C_p) at once; the Lean lemma is scalar, so one applies it five times — once per integrand — which is routine since under the paper's smoothness hypothesis all five integrands are continuous on [0,X]. The pressure row additionally needs the shared axis datum Π_ax, and `pressure_equal_after` supplies exactly that case. (b) Lean adds an explicit `ContinuousOn` hypothesis on [0,X] that the paper leaves to its standing smoothness assumption. `Witness.rows_outside` is listed only as a user of the conclusion, not as a statement of it: it is the five-row equality for one particular modulated-assembly witness, obtained from the structure field `v.restored` rather than from the general propagation, so it is an instance and not the general statement. No general five-row 'equal beyond X_h' declaration was found; `ModulatedProfileAssembly.rows_eq_of_nonnegative` is the nearest, and it assumes agreement on all of [0,X] rather than only on [X_h,X].
